messages:
Maria Li: Quick heads-up, I'm scheduling a full quantization perf sweep tomorrow AM. Need a strict runbook so results are reproducible and auditable.

Aj Patel: SGTM. What are the mandatory axes? kernels / batching / kv / calib / power?

Maria Li: All of the above. Draft checklist: single HF model checkpoint, explicit tokenizer version, three quant regimes (FP8, calibrated INT8, 4-bit), deterministic warmup, two power caps (100% and 80%), synthetic vs traffic-shaped batching, cold/warm/stale KV scenarios.

Sam Ortega: Add forced kernel selection toggles. We should run with kernel=A, kernel=B, and a "native" auto mode so we can measure the scheduler's picks.

Maria Li: Yes. Logs must include a KERNEL_MAP header with per-kernel timing. Example:

```
KERNEL_MAP: fused_attn_v3=85ms, nv_fmha=120ms, qkv_reorder=6ms
QUANT_REGIME: INT8
CALIBRATION_ID: 20260318-01
WARMUP_TOKENS: 128
```

Leo Zhang: Calibration details: use per-channel for weight tensors, per-tensor for activations. Persist calibration artifact path + sha256 + sample_count. Include sampled histograms for spot checks.

Aj Patel: I'll ensure calibration runner produces the proto and hash. Use the same calibration set for all INT8 runs to avoid cross-run variance.

perf-bot: Naming rule reminder: run name must encode quant_regime, kernel_tag, batch_profile, kv_state, e.g., `fp8_fused_realpoisson_warmkv`.

Sam Ortega: On batching: two profiles — "ideal" grouped-by-length batching, and "real" arrival shaped (Poisson arrivals with documented length distribution). Keep RNG seeds in metadata.

Maria Li: Arrival command we'll use:

```
python runner.py --arrival poisson --lambda 0.28 --len-dist p95_profile.json --duration 900 --seed 31415
```

Leo Zhang: KV scenarios: cold (KV cleared per request), hot (session-persistent cache), stale (cache from previous version). Stale should log a fallback flag and validation result.

Aj Patel: For output parity we run a deterministic eval harness: 500 prompts, temp=0, top_k=1, compare token-by-token with FP16 baseline. Log token-diffs + simple metrics (chr_err_rate, top1_agreement).

Maria Li: Warmup protocol: run 100 deterministic prefill iterations, then measure the next 200 iterations. If latency stddev > 3% we retry warmup once. If still >3% mark run unstable.

Sam Ortega: Abort criteria: latency variance >10% OR error rate >0.5% => mark run flaky and exclude from summary but keep artifacts for debugging.

perf-bot: Hardware counters to capture: GPU_util, GPU_power_W, mem_bw, SM_active, PCIe_bw. Include cgroup/cpu isolation flags used.

Leo Zhang: For mixed-precision/4-bit: capture fallback_count (ops executed in FP16/FP32 due to missing quant kernels) and sample up to 5 stack traces (PII scrubbed). Also record per-token fallback latency penalty.

Maria Li: We'll pin driver/runtime versions and enforce node isolation (no other tenants). Also flush OS caches and document kernel versions. Include a MANIFEST per run listing exact Docker image, git commit, and env vars.

Aj Patel: Golden run naming and manifest: each run should produce a tarball `<run_name>.tar.gz` containing logs/, hw_counters.csv, manifest.json (sha256), calibration_artifact, tokenizer.sha, eval_outputs.json.

Sam Ortega: Also measure scheduling overhead: time spent in batching/dispatch vs pure kernel execution. Include a small flame summary.

Maria Li: We'll require a small re-run script: `replay_run.py --run <run_name>` that pulls the artifacts and can re-run the same config in a single-node debug mode. Include that in tarball.

perf-bot: Placing scheduled job: 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z on queue `quant_full_sweep`. Notifications will post to #eng-runtime per batch.

Maria Li: Thanks — I'll land the checklist and the run manifest in the repo before midnight UTC. Expect first batch results by ~06:00Z. If anyone wants to change the window, ping me.

Aj Patel: Looks good. I'll own the runner changes.

Sam Ortega: I'll own kernel toggles and hw counter hooks.

Leo Zhang: I'll prepare the calibration set and histograms.

Maria Li: Awesome. We'll iterate on the output format if needed.
